The total causal effect of $X_{evo}$ on $G_{yzp}$ is the sum of the direct path ($X_{evo} \rightarrow G_{yzp}$) and the indirect path through $T_{ijv}$ ($X_{evo} \rightarrow T_{ijv} \rightarrow G_{yzp}$).

Since $X_{evo}$ is not a descendant of $T_{ijw}$, the path $X_{evo} \leftarrow \dots \rightarrow T_{ijw} \rightarrow G_{yzp}$ does not exist. The only paths from $X_{evo}$ to $G_{yzp}$ are the direct one and the indirect one through $T_{ijv}$. Method 1 captures the sum of these effects (the total effect), while Method 2 attempts to decompose it. Therefore, to assess the "how $X_{evo}$ affects $G_{yzp}$" (implying total effect), Method 1 is correct.
